text:
maria: Heads up — after landing the kernel-selector tweak yesterday I'm seeing a 2-3x spike in p95/p99 for long sequences on canary. Traces show a new hotspot that wasn't there before. Anyone else observing this?
jonathan: saw a small bump in telemetry too, particularly for seq >= 512. Can you drop an nsys link?
maria: Uploaded quick captures: before vs after (same model + inputs). Before: https://s3.internal.redwood/traces/3170004321/nsys-before.qd After: https://s3.internal.redwood/traces/3170004321/nsys-after.qd
kai: grabbing them now. Quick question — is this only on the fallback kernel path or also primary selection?
maria: looks like primary path still ok for short seqs. For long seqs the selector picks a fallback variant (memory-friendly) and the trace shows a huge spend in a kernel labelled fallback_gemm+prefetch.
olivia: can you paste the nvtx timeline snippet? a short screenshot or text is fine.
maria: pasted clipped timeline: ```
# simplified timeline (nsys)
0.00s  cuLaunchKernel main_gemm            0.48ms
0.48s  cuLaunchKernel main_gemm            0.52ms
...
1.20s  cuLaunchKernel fallback_gemm_prefetch 3.9ms  <-- new dominant span
1.24s  cudaMemcpyAsync                     0.12ms
```
jonathan: that fallback span looks like it's blocking other kernels (serializes warmup?). Could be a change in batching handoff or kernelheuristic threshold. Did the recent commit change prefetch window or tile size?
kai: I grepped the change — commit 3170087b touched kernel_selector.cc: it relaxed the occupancy threshold and added a fallback probe for mem-bound configs. Suspect it's choosing fallback for workloads that are better served by main_gemm.
maria: ran the same synthetic workload under perf and nsys with NVTX markers. Command I used: ```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx --output=run-after ./bench --model=bert --seq=768 --batch=1
```
olivia: nice. Can you run a before/after timeline diff with perfetto or the nsys export flamegraphs? A flame/stack diff would be convincing.
maria: attached flame SVGs (linked): before: https://s3.internal.redwood/traces/3170004321/flame-before.svg after: https://s3.internal.redwood/traces/3170004321/flame-after.svg — you can see large wedge for fallback_gemm_prefetch in after.
perf-bot: autotest-run: latency-regression flagged on canary. p99 increased from 72ms -> 198ms for seq=768. Ticket #INF-432 created.
jonathan: let's bisect to isolate the commit. Start range: good=3170002000 (last known good), bad=3170004321 (first bad). I'll kick off bisect on a local bench harness.
kai: quick tip — bisect with an automated harness that runs nsys-lite and checks for timeout or single-run p99 > 120ms. I have a script snippet: ```
git bisect start bad good
git bisect run ./tools/bisect_runner.sh --model bert --seq 768 --threshold 120
```
maria: ran a manual quick bisect locally — narrows to 3170087b as likely culprit (the selector changes). Reverting that commit locally returns p99 to ~70ms.
johnathan: small typo — that's jonathan :) But great. Can you paste the minimal repro and the revert patch?
maria: repro command (single-shot): ```
./bench --model bert --seq 768 --batch 1 --profile nsys --runs 5
# with bad commit: p99 ~198ms
# after revert: p99 ~74ms
```
olivia: good find. What's the root cause? Selector using occupancy model that underestimates main_gemm throughput for long sequences, so it chooses fallback (lower registered threads) which increases global serialization due to prefetch ordering.
kai: looking at kernel_selector.cc the new heuristic compares sm_efficiency < 0.65 and then probes fallback. For our long seq with kv-cache and large KV indices, measured sm_efficiency is noisy during warmup and drops below threshold -> triggers fallback. Need smoothing or stable probe windows.
maria: proposed fix: 1) add 3-sample EWMA to sm_efficiency before switching, 2) ensure probe doesn't run if active KV cache hits > X, 3) add unit benchmark that simulates long-seq latency and fails CI on regression. I'll open a PR.
perf-bot: CI perf-check scheduled — please attach nsys artifacts to PR for human review. See policy: https://intranet.redwood/dev/perf-policy
deploy-bot: canary rollback pending if revert PR merged. Ping @oncall if we need immediate rollback.
jonathan: can we add an alert to the console that tracks sudden increases in fallback kernel share per model+route? would help catch this class earlier.
olivia: yup — I'll add a per-model metric: fallback_kernel_ratio and a simple alert if it jumps > 20% in a 5m window.
maria: opened PR #5243 with EWMA smoothing and test harness, attached nsys before/after artifacts and perf measurements. CI runs now.
kai: after running local patched build + bench: p99 back to 78ms, flame looks like before. LGTM pending CI.
maria: final notes for postmortem: cause = over-aggressive kernel-selector fallback probe + noisy sm_efficiency metric during warmup; fix = smoothing + gating on KV hit-rate; follow-ups = alerting, nsys-based regression test, add perf-author checklist for kernel-selector changes. :white_check_mark:
jonathan: thanks all — great triage and speedy revert path.
olivia: adding postmortem stub to /docs/incidents once PR merges.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback canceled after PR merge.
